walkthroughs.body_html: In 1976, Brian O'Doherty published 'Inside the White Cube' in Artforum. He argued the modernist gallery's white walls, even light and exclusion of context were themselves ideological — not neutral but authoritative.
Curators choose hang height (often 145-150 cm to centre), sightlines, wall colour, label wording and lighting. Each is an editorial choice shaping how the work is read.
The black box — a darkened cinema-like room — has become standard for video art. It allows controlled projection but reproduces cinema's passive seated viewer, raising questions about gallery time.

mcqs.q: What is the idea behind the 'white cube' gallery space?
options: Neutral white walls aim to isolate art from distraction — though critics argue the format itself carries ideology.
White walls are simply the cheapest paint option.
White keeps the artworks cold for preservation.
No — curators only sell artworks.

mcqs.q: Why are works usually hung with their centres at a consistent height?
options: All frames must have their tops aligned instead.
It is required by fire regulations.
A consistent centre line at average eye level creates a coherent viewing experience.
White keeps the artworks cold for preservation.
